messages.content:
You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Creation and the patriarchs. People: Ancient Near Eastern households, herders and farmers. Dress: Simple wool or linen wraps, tunics and sandals. Buildings and objects: Wild land, tents, wells, altars and mud-brick towns as the text allows.

STORY SECTION: Destruction of the cities of the plain
ON STAGE: Lot's wife, Abram, Sodom, Gomorrah
TEXT OF THE SECTION'S FIRST MOMENT (the look covers the whole section):
Then Yahweh rained on Sodom and on Gomorrah sulfur and fire from Yahweh out of the sky.

You check an illustration plan before it is drawn. You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as a speaker, writer, prophet or listener put into a scene their words only describe or made a figure of their own words, the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.
For each problem, copy a short exact phrase from a scene field or a selected id into planQuote (from an owner constraint for look_conflict) and give a one-sentence reason.

You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as a speaker, writer, prophet or listener put into a scene their words only describe or made a figure of their own words, the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.
For each problem, copy a short exact phrase from a scene field or a selected id into planQuote (from an owner constraint for look_conflict) and give a one-sentence reason.

You plan one illustration of one moment of a work's text. You get the moment with its neighbours in the same story section, the work brief, the era, the section cast and a SECTION LOOK GUIDE. Return only JSON.
- Draw one scene at one instant: no collage and no sequence of steps. If the moment recounts several actions, pick one representative instant. If it has no event (a list, genealogy, law, saying or greeting), illustrate its content or setting through people, places and things, never as a written document.
- Show what the moment is about. When the moment is mostly someone's words (a prophecy, oracle, poem, proverb, prayer, letter, argument or teaching, or a story, parable, vision or memory being told), draw what the words describe and leave the speaker, writer and listeners out, unless the text shows them inside that scene (a visionary within the vision). Never put a speaker, writer or listener into a scene their words only describe, and never make them a figure of their own words, such as the king ready for battle or the man standing in the gap.
- In `selectedCast`, list every section cast entry that will be visible: people, groups, places, objects, and any presence without form shown through its effects. Give a few words of the text for each. Leave out cast who are elsewhere or only mentioned. Anyone without a cast entry may appear as an unnamed role or crowd when the moment needs them.
- Describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Leave fixed appearance to canon, name no art style, and ask for no visible writing: scrolls, tablets, letters and books stay rolled or closed, and signs and boards are blank. Describe only what can be seen; leave out unseen or invisible beings, because anything named gets drawn. Keep every depiction rule.
- The scene fields carry this moment's place, time, light and situational clothing. The SECTION LOOK GUIDE is a suggestion for them: keep what fits this moment and change what does not. OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS, when given instead, are binding: keep the setting and time of day consistent with them.
- Each field is one or two short phrases.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Creation and the patriarchs. People: Ancient Near Eastern households, herders and farmers. Dress: Simple wool or linen wraps, tunics and sandals. Technology: Hand tools, herding, farming and weighed metal; no modern objects.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement
People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples.
Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments.
Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.
Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Moses; The Israelite people (the children of Israel); the Egyptians

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- Red Sea: a wide, deep arm of open water between desert shores, its surface dark blue-green under wind. Sand dunes and low reddish cliffs line the coast; scattered tamarisk and palms grow at the water's edge. Bare rock outcrops and shallow wadis run down to the shore, and a distant fortified town sits on the northern ridge.
- The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.
- the Egyptians: adults of middle age, broad-shouldered and strong from labour and rank, with warm brown skin and close-cropped black hair, clean-shaven men with short wigs or bare heads, dignified and grave of face. Signature outfit: a pleated white linen kilt or wrap-tunic with a linen cloak in ochre and blue. Signature props: none carried alone; officers may bear a staff of office.
- Only Moses, Red Sea, The Israelite people (the children of Israel), the Egyptians have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Moses at the shore, arm stretched out over the sea, plain cloak and staff in hand
Action: Waters pulled back by a strong east wind, sea floor showing dry between two standing walls of water
Setting: Shore of the Red Sea at night, wilderness sand at the edges, parted waters rising on either side
Secondary elements: Israelite people gathered on the sand watching, a few Egyptian figures distant in linen, spray and dust lifted by the wind
Mood: Awe, tense hope and reverent wonder
Time of day: Night, toward the first grey of dawn, strong east wind, clouds moving fast
Composition: Wide view from the shore, Moses in the foreground at the left with arm extended, parted waters receding into the distance, radiance and cloud spread across the sky above the sea

ART STYLE: Fresco
Rendering: A finished early Renaissance fresco-style painting of the work's world: calm, monumental figures, clear gestures and simple architecture, painted in soft matte color.
Negatives: Show the scene itself, never a wall, plaster cracks, painted border, frame or ornamental band. No letters or inscriptions anywhere, and halos, if any, are plain. Avoid photorealism and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Soft earth reds, ochres, sage greens and pale lapis blue on light grounds.
Lighting: Even, gentle daylight with soft modelling and few cast shadows.
Materials and texture: Matte, chalky paint surface within the depicted world.
Composition: Balanced, legible staging with figures in a shallow space; the scene painted out to every edge and corner.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.

People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples.
Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments.
Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.
Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Moses; Aaron, brother of Moses

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.
- the camp of Israel: a wide wilderness encampment of dun-coloured tents of woven goat-hair cloth in ordered rows, with a central sanctuary tent and a gate; bare stony desert plain, scattered acacia and tamarisk, distant dark mountain slopes; a pillar of cloud above the camp by day and fire by night; ash-pits and a clean place beyond its edges.
- Only Moses, Aaron, brother of Moses, the camp of Israel have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Moses standing, one hand raised in instruction, beside Aaron in plain linen
Action: Moses teaches the people which animals are clean and unclean, pointing toward a pig set apart from the clean animals
Setting: Wilderness camp of Israel with tents and the tabernacle among desert rock and dry sand
Secondary elements: Israelite families gathered near the tents, a cloth-covered table with food, a pig set apart at the edge, a pillar of cloud above the tabernacle
Mood: Reverent, attentive and grounded, with a quiet sense of holy distinction
Time of day: Late afternoon in dry desert heat, warm low sun slanting over the camp
Composition: Wide view from the camp edge, Moses and Aaron in the foreground, the people and tents receding behind them

ART STYLE: Fresco
Rendering: A finished early Renaissance fresco-style painting of the work's world: calm, monumental figures, clear gestures and simple architecture, painted in soft matte color.
Negatives: Show the scene itself, never a wall, plaster cracks, painted border, frame or ornamental band. No letters or inscriptions anywhere, and halos, if any, are plain. Avoid photorealism and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Soft earth reds, ochres, sage greens and pale lapis blue on light grounds.
Lighting: Even, gentle daylight with soft modelling and few cast shadows.
Materials and texture: Matte, chalky paint surface within the depicted world.
Composition: Balanced, legible staging with figures in a shallow space; the scene painted out to every edge and corner.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

You inspect a finished illustration for four visible faults before a reader sees it. Judge only from the image. Return only JSON.
The scene should show: The Israelite people (the children of Israel); The priests and Levites (Deuteronomy); Joshua son of Nun. Its description: A crowd of Israelite warriors and families surging forward over a collapsed section of stone wall; Priests in linen robes near the front blowing long trumpets; scattered fallen stones and dust; Jericho's mudbrick towers standing at the edges
- figure_in_light: true if any face, head, hands, robe, body or human-shaped silhouette appears inside, made of or emerging from light, radiance, cloud, smoke, fire, a pillar or the sky, or seated or standing on a throne, unless it is clearly one of the beings the description names. You check an illustration plan before it is drawn. You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as a speaker, writer, prophet or listener put into a scene their words only describe or made a figure of their own words, the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. 2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.

Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist and a rough brown wool cloak in earth tones. Carries a simple wooden staff, the sign of a traveling prophet.
- Seraphim: a heavenly being of tall, luminous human-like form, ageless, with burnished bronze-gold skin. Six wings: two cover the face, two cover the feet, two lift in flight, feathered in white and gold. Face hidden behind the wings. Robed in a long linen tunic of pale white. - Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

You check an illustration plan before it is drawn. You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as a speaker, writer, prophet or listener put into a scene their words only describe or made a figure of their own words, the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.

Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.

Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.

Kinds:

The city appearing on the horizon belongs to the next moment, not this one, since the new heaven and earth comes first and the city's descent happens afterward — so new_jerusalem should also be outside_instant, with the plan quote referencing where the city appears. The radiant cloud and light are fine as setting details without needing embodiment. I'm ready to output the single-line JSON result.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Visionary heaven and renewal
People: Seers, heavenly beings and the redeemed as described.
Dress: Robes and garments with the text's colors and materials.
Buildings and objects: Thrones, altars, glass-like sea and jeweled city as described.
Technology: Ancient lamps, trumpets, harps, swords and sailing ships; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Four living creatures (Revelation)

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Four living creatures: ageless and powerful, each with six wings set close about the body; the wings and bodies are covered with eyes, around and within. One is lion-like with a mane of tawny gold, one calf-like with a sleek red-brown hide, one with a human face of grave dignity and dark skin, one eagle-like with bronze-gold feathers. Robes of deep crimson and white.
- Heavenly throne room: a vast open sanctuary of radiance beneath a heaven like crystal, floored with a sea of glass that is clear as crystal, set with a great throne and a temple whose doors open onto the heavens, lit by lightnings, thunders and a rainbow the colour of emerald about the throne. Pale gold and white stone, jasper and sardius glimmer in the walls; an altar of gold stands before the throne.
- Only Four living creatures (Revelation), Heavenly throne room have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Four fearsome living creatures standing in the middle of and around the throne, their bodies covered in eyes before and behind
Action: They stand fixed and watchful, gazing outward in every direction, while radiance flows from the throne.
Setting: A vast heavenly throne room with a sea of glass like crystal stretching before the throne, glowing with reflected light.
Secondary elements: A rim of radiant light and cloud around the throne, faint mist rising from the glassy sea, with lightnings and thunders and a rainbow like an emerald about the throne.
Mood: Awe, reverence and solemn watchfulness.
Time of day: Timeless heavenly light, unchanging, with still, clear air and a rainbow arching about the throne.
Composition: A wide view of the throne room from slightly below, centering the throne and the creatures with the glassy sea spread in the foreground.

ART STYLE: Fresco
Rendering: A finished early Renaissance fresco-style painting of the work's world: calm, monumental figures, clear gestures and simple architecture, painted in soft matte color.
Negatives: Show the scene itself, never a wall, plaster cracks, painted border, frame or ornamental band. No letters or inscriptions anywhere, and halos, if any, are plain. Avoid photorealism and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Soft earth reds, ochres, sage greens and pale lapis blue on light grounds.
Lighting: Even, gentle daylight with soft modelling and few cast shadows.
Materials and texture: Matte, chalky paint surface within the depicted world.
Composition: Balanced, legible staging with figures in a shallow space; the scene painted out to every edge and corner.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

You plan one illustration of one moment of a work's text. You get the moment with its neighbours in the same story section, the work brief, the era, the section cast and a SECTION LOOK GUIDE. Return only JSON.
- Draw one scene at one instant: no collage and no sequence of steps. If the moment recounts several actions, pick one representative instant. If it has no event (a list, genealogy, law, saying or greeting), illustrate its content or setting through people, places and things, never as a written document.
- Show what the moment is about. When the moment is mostly someone's words (a prophecy, oracle, poem, proverb, prayer, letter, argument or teaching, or a story, parable, vision or memory being told), draw what the words describe and leave the speaker, writer and listeners out, unless the text shows them inside that scene (a visionary within the vision). Never put a speaker, writer or listener into a scene their words only describe, and never make them a figure of their own words, such as the king ready for battle or the man standing in the gap.
- In `selectedCast`, list every section cast entry that will be visible: people, groups, places, objects, and any presence without form shown through its effects. Give a few words of the text for each. Leave out cast who are elsewhere or only mentioned. Anyone without a cast entry may appear as an unnamed role or crowd when the moment needs them.
- Describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Leave fixed appearance to canon, name no art style, and ask for no visible writing: scrolls, tablets, letters and books stay rolled or closed, and signs and boards are blank. Describe only what can be seen; leave out unseen or invisible beings, because anything named gets drawn. Keep every depiction rule.
- The scene fields carry this moment's place, time, light and situational clothing. The SECTION LOOK GUIDE is a suggestion for them: keep what fits this moment and change what does not. OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS, when given instead, are binding: keep the setting and time of day consistent with them.
- Each field is one or two short phrases.
- Cast marked hasForm: false have no body and are never drawn. When the moment shows one of them appearing or acting, select it and show the moment through the place and the people who witness it. In the scene fields, describe in your own plain words only the physical effects the text names, such as smoke, cloud, fire, storm, wind or light filling a place, spread through the scene or coming from beyond the frame rather than gathered into one glowing shape. Never name it or call it seated, standing, enthroned or riding, and leave out its throne, seat, chariot, robe, train or hem and any face, hands, hair or body: bodily words in the text are metaphors. Say only where those effects are. Whenever the scene keeps light, cloud or fire that comes from it, select it. Keep the people and the place as the subject of the image. A command, oath or mention alone is not an appearance, so add no effect for it then.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Visionary heaven and renewal. People: Seers, heavenly beings and the redeemed as described. Dress: Robes and garments with the text's colors and materials. Technology: Ancient lamps, trumpets, harps, swords and sailing ships; no modern objects.
STORY SECTION: New heaven and new earth

MOMENT (Revelation 21:1): I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth have passed away, and the sea is no more.
PREVIOUS: (section starts here)
NEXT: I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.

CAST ON STAGE IN THIS SECTION (id: name):
- god_yahweh_the_father_and_god_of_israel: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel (hasForm: false)
- new_jerusalem: New Jerusalem (hasForm: true)

SECTION LOOK GUIDE (a suggestion; keep what fits this moment):

A PREVIOUS PLAN FOR THIS MOMENT WAS REJECTED. Write a new plan that fixes every problem below and keeps what was correct:
- outside_instant: The seer is the narrator of the vision ('I saw'), and the plan places this narrator as a figure in the scene. (plan said: "A seer standing in the foreground")

You check an illustration plan before it is drawn. You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as a speaker, writer, prophet or listener put into a scene their words only describe or made a figure of their own words, the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.
